tony: Are we changing the quickstart snippets or the deeper tuning guide (or both)?

maya: Both. Quickstart gets a compact drop-in example for batching. Tuning guide gets the migration checklist + decision heuristics for choosing profiles.

liam: Please add a minimal SDK batched-call example. Support keeps seeing customers sending one-off sequential requests instead of batching. A tiny snippet fixes a lot of tickets.

maya: added Python + JS snippets in the draft. Python:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
prompts = ["Summarize: ...", "Summarize: ..."]
resp = client.generate(model="rw1-quant-v2", prompts=prompts, max_tokens=120, batch_size=2)
print(resp.texts)
```
JS:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood()
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw1-quant-v2', prompts: ['A','B'], max_tokens: 120, batch_size: 2 })
console.log(resp.outputs)
```

emily: looks good. two asks: 1) add one sentence on when batching is preferred vs streaming (latency vs throughput), and 2) fix the broken quant-profiles anchor we moved last week.

tony: For the migration checklist, suggest a tiny decision tree:
- cost priority -> start with int8 profile A
- quality priority -> use int8+KV or fp16 fallback
- heavy caching -> allow more aggressive quant but validate on your prompt set

liam: also add a lightweight eval snippet to run a prompt set against the new profile and report avg latency + basic quality metric. that helped sales catch regressions last quarter.

maya: adding a small python eval snippet to the draft that records avg latency: 
```python
from redwood import Client
import time
client = Client(model='rw1-quant-v3')
prompts = open('eval_prompts.txt').read().splitlines()
latencies = []
for p in prompts:
    t0 = time.time()
    resp = client.generate(prompt=p, max_tokens=50)
    latencies.append(time.time()-t0)
print('avg_latency', sum(latencies)/len(latencies))
```

emily: could we include a line about tokenization differences and a rollback threshold? e.g., "if quality metric regresses >3% revert or try fp16 fallback."

maya: added: "If eval shows >3% quality regression on your primary metric, revert and try fp16 or a narrower quant profile."

tony: add a short KV-cache compatibility note — older kernels sometimes needed a cache-warmup tweak. include the ops curl we used: 
```bash
# warm up KV cache to stabilize latency
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw1-quant-v3","prompt":"Warmup: hello","max_tokens":1}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
